slot.brief: Two fixed point charges a given distance apart; find where along the line a third charge must be placed so the net force on it is zero.

stem: Two fixed charges, $+4\ \mu\text{C}$ and $+1\ \mu\text{C}$, are $30$ cm apart. How far from the $+4\ \mu\text{C}$ charge should a nonzero third charge be placed between them so that the net force on it is zero?

verdicts.working: Between the charges, the electric fields oppose. Set their magnitudes equal: \(4/x^2=1/(30-x)^2\), giving \(x=20\) cm from the \(+4\ \mu\text{C}\) charge.

working:
Let $x$ be the distance from the $+4\ \mu\text{C}$ charge.
$$\frac{k(4)}{x^2}=\frac{k(1)}{(30-x)^2}$$
$$\frac{2}{x}=\frac{1}{30-x}\quad\Rightarrow\quad x=20\text{ cm}$$

Independent check: Between the charges, the electric fields oppose. Set their magnitudes equal: \(4/x^2=1/(30-x)^2\), giving \(x=20\) cm from the \(+4\ \mu\text{C}\) charge.
solution:
Between the charges, the electric fields oppose. For zero net force, their magnitudes must be equal:
$$\frac{k(4)}{x^2}=\frac{k(1)}{(30-x)^2}\quad\Rightarrow\quad \frac{2}{x}=\frac{1}{30-x}$$
Solving gives $x=20\text{ cm}$ from the $+4\,\mu\text{C}$ charge.
